source_note: Article numbers and titles reference Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR). The 'text' field is an original, concise paraphrase written for this proof-of-concept, NOT the verbatim legal text of the Regulation. Consult the official Regulation for authoritative wording.

requirements.title: Principles relating to processing of personal data
requirements.text: Personal data must be processed lawfully, fairly and transparently; collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes; minimized; accurate; kept no longer than necessary; and processed securely, with the controller accountable for demonstrating compliance.

requirements.title: Lawfulness of processing
requirements.text: Processing is lawful only if at least one legal basis applies, such as consent, contract necessity, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, or legitimate interests.

requirements.title: Right of access by the data subject
requirements.text: Data subjects have the right to obtain confirmation of whether their personal data is processed and, where it is, access to that data and information about the processing.

requirements.title: Right to erasure ('right to be forgotten')
requirements.text: Data subjects have the right to obtain erasure of their personal data without undue delay where defined grounds apply, and controllers must take reasonable steps to inform other processors.

requirements.title: Data protection by design and by default
requirements.text: Controllers must implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to embed data-protection principles into processing, and by default process only data necessary for each specific purpose.

requirements.title: Records of processing activities
requirements.text: Controllers and processors must maintain a written record of processing activities under their responsibility, including purposes, categories of data and recipients, transfers, and security measures.

requirements.title: Security of processing
requirements.text: Controllers and processors must implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, including pseudonymization, encryption, confidentiality, integrity, availability, resilience, and regular testing.

requirements.title: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority
requirements.text: Controllers must notify the competent supervisory authority of a personal data breach without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to individuals.

requirements.title: Communication of a personal data breach to the data subject
requirements.text: When a breach is likely to result in a high risk to individuals, the controller must communicate the breach to affected data subjects without undue delay, describing the nature and likely consequences.

requirements.title: Data protection impact assessment
requirements.text: Where processing is likely to result in a high risk to individuals, the controller must carry out a data protection impact assessment before processing, evaluating risks and mitigating measures.
